clue.text: Underline a kind of pressure

definitions.meaning: to underline a point is to emphasise it
a force or strain applied to a material, or mental strain

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of weight placed on something: emphasis on a point, or strain on a body.

clue.text: Dappled bird completely plucked?

parts.note: pie is an old name for the magpie, still used in crosswords
a bird with every feather plucked is left bald

explanation.surface: A mottled bird ends up stripped of all its feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Patched in two colours, especially black and white, like a horse's coat.

clue.text: Holy man needing someone to darn his holey socks?

definitions.text: Holy man needing someone to darn his holey socks?

parts.words: Holy man needing someone to darn his holey socks?
parts.note: a begging monk, with the first word of his title heard as '...', so he needs someone else to darn for him

explanation.surface: A monk with worn-out socks is looking for someone handy with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'dam', a misread of 'darn' (to mend a hole by weaving). 'Holey' puns on 'holy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a religious order that lives by begging, such as a Franciscan.

clue.text: Hag ridden sweepers

parts.note: brushes made of twigs, the kind a witch is pictured riding through the sky

explanation.surface: Cleaners tormented by a nagging old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hag-ridden' usually means harassed or plagued; here it means literally ridden by a hag, a witch on her broomstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Twig brooms, the traditional mount of storybook witches.

clue.text: Country stay with an academic leader

parts.note: a guy is a rope that stays or steadies a tent or mast
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from academic

explanation.surface: A nation is told to keep company with the head of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation on the Atlantic coast, formerly British Guiana.

clue.text: Old convicts on a wild goose chase?

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but the chase is after several of the birds, so the answer is plural

parts.note: grey hair goes with old age
lag is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: Elderly prisoners are sent off on a hopeless pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The species of grey goose native to Europe, ancestor of the farmyard goose.

clue.text: Why one hears chat about a craft

indicators.note: the solver is told to listen, so the word why is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

indicators.note: the letters of chat are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why they overhear gossip about a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel used for pleasure or racing, craft being a general word for a boat.

clue.text: Agreeable feature in scenes reproduced

indicators.note: produced again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant quality shows up in scenes that are copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantness, the quality of being agreeable.

clue.text: Score in duplicate

parts.note: a score is twenty, and twenty is a smaller number given two times over

explanation.surface: A result written down twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lots of ten make twenty, which is a score.

clue.text: The bird for a firm to carp about

indicators.note: the nagging word is placed about, outside, the letters for a firm

parts.note: to carp at someone is to peck at them, nag
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company takes the bird as its emblem to complain about.
explanation.definitionFit: The male peafowl, known for its showy fanned tail.

clue.text: Place in a way taking me back to the cradle

indicators.note: taking the word me back means reading it in reverse

parts.note: a cradle is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: Someone is put back into a baby's cot.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something firmly within surrounding material.

clue.text: Heavy burden that goes against the grain

definitions.meaning: a load round one's neck, a responsibility that weighs one down
a grinding stone turns against the corn to make flour

explanation.definitionFit: A grinding wheel in a flour mill, and the figurative weight hung round one's neck.

clue.text: Sprite turning sanctimonious around noon

indicators.note: turning the built word means reading it backwards
the sanctimonious word goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious
M stands for meridies, Latin for midday, as in a.m. and p.m.

explanation.surface: A fairy becomes self-righteous at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous devil or goblin.

clue.text: An incongruity for exclusive ones in the Common Market

parts.note: sole rights are exclusive rights

indicators.note: the ones are placed inside the market letters

parts.note: C and M are the initials of Common Market
I is the roman numeral one, so ones are I's

explanation.surface: Exclusive members inside the European trading bloc look out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical mistake or breach of etiquette, something out of keeping.

clue.text: Showy and somewhat vulgar I should say

indicators.note: only some of the words vulgar I should are used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a display is flashy and rather crude.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed page drops the 'I'; the run vulGAR I SHould needs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish colours are loud, tastelessly bright.

clue.text: Recognise and take into custody

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from seizing: grasping an idea, or seizing a person under arrest.

clue.text: Ireland as it was once

parts.note: the classical Latin name given to the island by the Romans

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for Ireland, used poetically.

clue.text: Marshal of France with a hankering to retreat

parts.note: a yen is a longing or hankering

explanation.surface: A French military leader yearns to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals, called 'the bravest of the brave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel Ney, Napoleonic commander given the rank of Marshal of the Empire.

clue.text: To cut off gives alien an eye-opener

parts.note: the opener of the word eye is its first letter
alien and strange both mean unfamiliar

explanation.surface: Cutting someone off gives a foreigner a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-opener' looks like a surprise but means the opening letter of 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, separating someone from former friends.

clue.text: Striking creature a Ptolemy queen finally embraced

definitions.text: Striking creature a Ptolemy queen finally embraced

parts.words: Striking creature a Ptolemy queen finally embraced
parts.note: Cleopatra, last queen of the Ptolemy dynasty, died by holding a venomous snake to her breast

explanation.surface: An Egyptian queen's last embrace is with a deadly snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Egyptian cobra said to have killed Cleopatra.

clue.text: Turns four vessels round

indicators.note: the vessels go round the number

parts.note: pots are vessels
IV is four in roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone spins four containers round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivots as a verb means swivels or turns on a point.

clue.text: Grow old in a genteel way

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words a genteel

explanation.surface: Advice to become elderly gracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older.

clue.text: Deposited in imposing style

explanation.definitionFit: Placed up on top, and treated unfairly by others who take advantage.

clue.text: Persuade complete eighteen holes

definitions.meaning: a full round of golf has eighteen holes

explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone, and to finish a full circuit of a golf course.

clue.text: Slips into Latin

parts.note: mistakes, put into the Latin word used for a list of printing errors

explanation.definitionFit: A Latin plural meaning errors, used for a list of corrections in a book.

clue.text: Cowboy employed on the golf course

definitions.meaning: a club used for long tee shots

explanation.definitionFit: A drover of cattle, and the long-hitting golf club.

clue.text: May well be a former rep artist

indicators.note: the words could well turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor might once have been a repertory player.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer such as an actor or musician.

clue.text: See 3
Female most alluring at I a.m.?

definitions.text: Female most alluring at I a.m.?

parts.words: Female most alluring at I a.m.?
parts.note: a nymph of paradise, seen as a word for a time of day followed by I, so one o'clock

explanation.definitionFit: A beautiful maiden of the Muslim paradise, hence any alluring woman.

clue.text: State for Asian with a following

indicators.note: the a comes following the Asian, after it

parts.note: an Indian is an Asian

explanation.surface: An Asian has a band of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Midwest, capital Indianapolis.

clue.text: Open carriage phaetons replaced

indicators.note: the letters of phaetons are put back in a different place

explanation.surface: Old horse-drawn carriages are swapped for new ones.
explanation.walkthrough: A phaeton is itself a light carriage, so the surface stays in the stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open horse-drawn carriage with one seat, named after a clergyman.

clue.text: Fence not right for Peter Pan's creator

indicators.note: the right letter is not there, taken away

parts.note: a fence is a barrier

explanation.surface: A fence is wrong for the writer of a children's classic.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, Scottish playwright who wrote Peter Pan.
